extraction.Name: Alice M. Sasse
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent in fee to her 160 acre allotment at the time she got it; but, on October 19, 1918, Superintendent Tidwell, of the Indian Agency, at Pine Ridge, South Dakota, addressed her a letter, stating that she would better take her patent, that it was reported to the Tax Collector, and she would have to pay taxes on it at any rate
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: about 1921, she sold her 160 acre allotment to George Dixon, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $1250.00 cash
extraction.Buyer: George Dixon, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $1250.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she did not consider it a fair price for the land, but that she took it rather than have the taxes eat up the value of the land
extraction.Occupation/Income: husband supports his family through farming; and that this is his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has good health for the most part; has five minor children who have good health; husband's health is not so good; has never received any help from the County or Government; document dated November 19, 1928; letter from Superintendent Tidwell dated October 19, 1918
